generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The old `VersionCompatibilityChecks` in `org.elasticsearch.xpack.ql.index` is deleted and a new one is created in `org.elasticsearch.xpack.sql.index`. The new version correctly delegates to `VersionCompatibility` in the proto package. However, note that the new class no longer exposes `INTRODUCING_UNSIGNED_LONG`, `INTRODUCING_UNSIGNED_LONG_TRANSPORT`, or `INTRODUCING_VERSION_FIELD_TYPE` as constants. Callers that previously imported these from the old class (e.g., `Querier`, `CompositeKeyExtractor`) now import them from `VersionCompatibility` directly. This is fine, but ensure no remaining callers still reference the old package path.

`BaseRestSqlTestCase` duplicates the `getServerCompatVersion()` logic that already exists in `org.elasticsearch.xpack.sql.action.SqlVersionUtils`. Instead of re-implementing the try/catch fallback, this class should simply use `SqlVersionUtils.SERVER_COMPAT_VERSION`. This avoids a maintenance trap where the two implementations could diverge.

`UNSIGNED_LONG_TEST_VERSIONS` and `VERSION_FIELD_TEST_VERSIONS` are declared as `public static` but missing the `final` modifier. They should be `public static final` to prevent accidental reassignment and to match the convention used for similar constants elsewhere in the codebase.

`getAllVersions()` returns the internal mutable `ArrayList` directly. Callers (e.g., `VersionParityTests`, `SqlVersionTests`) could inadvertently mutate the shared list. Consider returning `Collections.unmodifiableList(DECLARED_VERSIONS)` or storing an unmodifiable list in `DECLARED_VERSIONS`.

The `isClientCompatible` method now short-circuits to `true` for any client ≥ `INTRODUCING_VERSIONING_INDEPENDENT_FEATURES` (8.16.0), regardless of the server version. This is a significant semantic change from the previous logic which required `server >= client`. The test `testVersionCompatibilityClientVersionIndependentFeatures` only validates the case where both server and client are ≥ 8.16.0. Consider adding a test that explicitly verifies a client ≥ 8.16.0 is deemed compatible with a server < 8.16.0, to document this intentional behavior and prevent accidental regression.

The conversions `Version.fromId(INTRODUCING_UNSIGNED_LONG.id)` and `TransportVersion.fromId(INTRODUCING_UNSIGNED_LONG.id)` rely on the id encoding being identical across `SqlVersion`, `Version`, and `TransportVersion`. This is a fragile coupling — if the id schemes ever diverge, these calls would silently produce wrong versions. Consider adding a comment at each call site noting this assumption, or (better) introducing a dedicated `TransportVersion`/`Version` constant in `VersionCompatibility` to make the dependency explicit.

review_comment: main is now v9, which can only talk to 8.17 nodes (when released). Does this mean we can remove all these versions, or are these actually _client_ versions which still need to be compatible? Is this documented somewhere?

> Is this documented somewhere?

The  the current version compatibility policy has been documented [here](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/sql-jdbc.html#jdbc-compatibility). This has been applying to the 7.x and 8.x.

Given the SQL maintenance status, this PR proposes updating this policy by allowing unrestricted connectivity between clients and servers past 8.16 (comment [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/112094/files#diff-35b51352875c23b3a8029fab7ad54b93bb9363c8d5a14bfd61992a534a3e86edR28-R32)). Any pre-8.16 releases (including all 8.15 releases to follow) will have to comply with the exiting policy (linked above).
The SL releases will be considered at version 8.16 (the "server compatibility version").

> Does this mean we can remove all these versions.

The versions should remain in the 8.x branch, but those 7.x not referenced explicitly in `VersionCompatibility` class (I think it's just `SqlVersions.V_7_12_0`) could be removed on 9.x. I think this would be done after back porting to 8.x though.

> are these actually client versions which still need to be compatible?

Yes, the post 7.7.0 client releases would need to stay compatible with 8.x servers.

> those 7.x not referenced explicitly in VersionCompatibility class (I think it's just SqlVersions.V_7_12_0) could be removed on 9.x

This could be an `@UpdateForV9` tag on the 7.0.0 version/SqlVersion class.

I think it's worth a descriptive comment at this point, that no further versions should be added in the normal course of things.
